internal/secrets/write.go: the sealed payload (ciphertext and tag) is written to the provider before any metadata version is published, preceded by a provider-independent CAS pre-check, so a stale, duplicate or conflicted write cannot reach the provider payload store and no metadata version can exist without provider-owned bytes.

results.domain_engine: bounded authorized reveal implemented and verified on the real local storage/provider/auth boundaries

verification_details.no_store: RevealResponse.NoStoreHeaders sets Cache-Control: no-store, Pragma: no-cache, Expires: 0 and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff; the acceptance test writes the response through httptest.ResponseRecorder and asserts every header plus a single streaming body write, and WriteResponse destroys the transient buffer.
verification_details.step_up_ordering: auth.AuthorizeProviderAction validates the fresh step-up grant, session binding, owner, canonical path, vault binding, forged headers and mapped provider scope before reveal reads metadata or calls the provider; tests assert the provider decrypt/read call budget stays 0 for every guard case.
verification_details.redaction: RevealedPlaintext redacts String, GoString, Format (all verbs including %x and %q) and MarshalJSON; RevealResponse String, GoString and MarshalJSON are redacted and AuditContent carries only action, actor, vault, path, version, classification and outcome. Tests assert the canary never appears in the formatted response, the serialized response, the audit projection or any failure message, and that Destroy zeroes the buffer.
verification_details.provider_ownership: The sealed bytes (ciphertext and tag) live only in the provider KV v2 path <vault>/<secret path>/v<version>; exhaustive scans assert the canary never appears in committed metadata, in the provider-owned sealed bytes or in any file under the storage directory, and that the provider payload is written before the metadata version is published.
verification_details.write_conflict_semantics: The payload write is create-only (cas=0). A CAS pre-check rejects stale and duplicate writes before the provider is called, and a provider conflict re-reads the authoritative record: an advanced record is reported as STALE_VERSION (concurrency loser), otherwise the conflict is surfaced as PROVIDER_CONFLICT with no metadata version published.
verification_details.restart_recovery: The acceptance test closes and reopens the authoritative store and reveals the committed version through the provider again, returning the rotated plaintext.

observed_limitations: The bounded reveal response is a domain/transport contract consumed through RevealResponse; no public or private engine HTTP endpoint is exposed by this task (W06/W07 own the engine API and UI wiring), so the accepted output is not yet reachable from the browser.

A crash between the provider payload write and the metadata publication leaves a provider-owned payload version with no metadata reference. Reveal can never reach it (it is metadata-driven) and the next attempt is refused with PROVIDER_CONFLICT instead of overwriting bytes; reconciliation is deferred to the recovery task C24 and documented here rather than faked.
The version-scoped provider path is read as its latest KV version, which is always the payload matched to the committed metadata envelope because a conflicting or stale write cannot overwrite it.
Payload and reveal sizes are bounded at 1 MiB (secrets.MaxSecretBytes, provider.MaxSealedPayloadBytes); larger inputs fail closed with a typed error.

The working tree is not committed. CI jobs that inspect a checkout (source integrity, runtime-engine) require the owner's approval to commit the listed paths, including the newly visible internal/secrets package.
rollback_or_recovery_observation: Reverting the isolated source change restores the previous behavior; no incompatible data was accepted. If a partial write ever leaves an unreferenced provider payload version, the public state remains the last committed metadata version and forward repair (provider reconciliation) is required before another write of that version can succeed; no older accepted state is overwritten by a backup.
